description: Our goal is to build a game where players manage resources, face the unknown and turn a barren rock into a home. We're here to learn fast, build together and ship something we're proud of before the deadline.
summary:
We made an intuitive and realistic Martian space colony simulator, where every decision matters. In the hostile environment of Mars, you’ll have to contend with storms, micrometeorites, radiation, limited material and vital supplies.
This game introduces the youngh to the real challenges NASA faces.
details:
Our game is a strategy colony simulator that puts players in charge of a real Mars outpost mission. Instead of treating Mars as a sandbox with unlimited resources, the game makes players face the real constraints of living there, such like limited power, scarce water and oxygen, dangerous environmental threats, and dependence on Earth for resupply.

Every decision has a tangible consequence. If players expand their buildings without considering the electrical and resource impact, the base falls into a power deficit, systems shut down, and they cannot act until the next scheduled cargo arrives from Earth. Before landing, players choose which astronauts to bring, so crew skills become part of the strategy. They must also respond to emergencies like tunnel breaches, which they must repair. Resupply rockets arrive only in scheduled launch windows with a limited cargo mass. Players must decide what is worth sending, because items such as electronic chips can only come from Earth.

Benefits and intended impact

The game teaches players, especially young people, the engineering trade-offs behind a Mars base: power budgeting, life-support dependencies, logistics, and resource management. Players learn why a Mars mission is hard by living through the consequences of their own choices, not by reading facts. We want to inspire curiosity about space exploration and help the next generation of explorers think like mission planners.

Tools and technologies

Godot Engine 4: the 3D game engine for gameplay, simulation systems, and UI.

Blender: all 3D assets, modeled by our team.

FL Studio: original music composed for the game.

Codex: AI coding assistance, which sped up development while the team designed and reviewed the systems.

Creativity

Our creativity lies in turning mission constraints into the core gameplay. Power deficits, launch windows, mass-limited cargo manifests, and Earth-only supplies are the challenge itself. We also made every asset ourselves, including the models and the soundtrack, so the whole experience is original.

Factors the team considered

Realism vs. fun: realistic constraints that stay understandable for a young audience.

Education: clear feedback so players can see why something failed and how to fix it.

Scope: a small, focused feature set that could be finished and polished in a short development time.

Accessibility: a fixed isometric camera with simple controls (rotate, zoom, WASD) and adjustable game speed.

Threats: environmental dangers only, since the focus is the real challenges of a Mars mission.
